step5_backupPolicy.status: SURFACED, NOT DECIDED — standing rule 7 (backup before every batch) stands; this batch took its full backup the old way.
step5_backupPolicy.question: Replace the per-batch full-schema backup (design-system-schema.backup-<date>-pre-<batch>.json, 1.4 MB each, 89 files today) with immutable records + git + generated-aggregate verification + milestone snapshots?

options.option: A — keep per-batch full backups (status quo)
options.tradeoffs: Zero policy change and the recovery path every past record describes. Cost: 1.4 MB per batch that grows with the register, 89 near-duplicate files already in the root, and the backup copies the generated aggregate rather than the store, so it no longer protects the thing that is edited.

options.option: B — immutable records + git + milestone snapshots (the plan's proposal)
options.tradeoffs: Recovery becomes git (every record file is committed and never rewritten; validate-split refuses a changed DONE record) plus a tagged snapshot at milestones (e.g. schema-split-baseline-2026-09-08) instead of a copy per batch. Cost: recovery depends on committing at batch close (OPERATORS.md already requires it); an uncommitted working tree has no backup until the record is committed; the standing rule 7 text and every apply script template change.

options.option: C — per-batch backup of the store instead of the aggregate (transitional)
options.tradeoffs: Keeps a backup per batch but of what is actually edited: a zip or a tagged commit of records/, flags/, foundation/ before each batch. Cost: still one artefact per batch; a tag is only useful if committed; a zip is not diffable.

step5_backupPolicy.recommendation: B with a milestone tag at every commit that closes a batch (the finish gate could create it), after the operator confirms; until then A stands.
